description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support or product-feasibility decisions, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iPadOS with optional Apple Pencil. Notebook disables typing whenever Pencil is nearby, makes handwriting the only way to enter specimen IDs and uses one gesture to both erase ink and delete a whole page. Text boxes are custom canvases.

# Apple HIG: Map user actions to input and alternatives

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the action and available hardware/input context, then enter the keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controller, Pencil, Crown or sensor procedure.
2. Preserve reserved system gestures and familiar input meanings. Separate targeting, focus, selection and activation; define feedback and reachable alternatives for the actions people must complete.
3. Account for comfort, precision, fatigue and switching between available inputs. Custom inputs should not remove an accessible route to an essential action.
4. Deliver an action-to-input mapping, focus/selection states and observable verification scenarios. Keep code/static observations separate from physical comfort, eye/hand and hardware checks.

name: apple-hig-apple-pencil-and-scribble
description: Use when designing or reviewing iPad Pencil drawing, hover, double tap, squeeze, barrel roll, Scribble, or mixed handwriting and control interaction.
---

# Keep drawing immediate and handwriting stable

Read [Apple Pencil and Scribble](../../references/apple-pencil-and-scribble.md). Inspect the iPad task, drawing/text areas, tools, supported Pencil features, and supplied implementation. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Preserve the chosen framework; feature availability depends on the Pencil/device, not merely iPadOS support.

Separate marking from text entry. Marking should begin immediately, including useful margins, and feedback should follow the touched content. Ordinary controls must remain Pencil-activatable. Map pressure/tilt/roll to continuous mark qualities where meaningful, keeping controls clear of either hand. For fixed photos/PDFs, preserve annotation visibility rather than automatically changing ink colors with appearance.

Treat hover as prediction, never activation: show a representative likely mark without distracting height-driven changes. Respect preferred double-tap tool mappings; any custom behavior should be opt-in, discoverable, nondestructive, and reversible. Squeeze is one quick action with UI near the tip, not sustained/repeated pressure. Reserve barrel roll for marks, not navigation.

For Scribble, accept writing without an extra focus tap where supported, provide enough space before entry or during a pause, hide placeholders when writing starts, and keep the field/transcription stationary mid-stroke. Password fields are an exception to automatic handwriting support. Supply undo/redo routes when a compact tool picker lacks them.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a diagram tool requires selecting Pen before every margin note, uses hover to commit dots, and moves a label field as letters appear. Decision: marking must be immediate and handwriting spatially stable. After, margin strokes draw directly, hover previews only, and label resizing waits until writing pauses; reversible tool changes respect Pencil preferences.

Deliver revised tool/input states or implementation. Fail if hover changes content, accidental squeeze deletes work, strokes lag behind detached feedback, or Scribble targets move during entry. Qualify latency, palm/hand comfort, hover, and hardware gesture claims until actual iPad/Pencil execution.

Use [Gestures](../apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md) for shared gesture alternatives and [Typography](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) for transcribed-text reflow.

name: apple-hig-keyboards
description: Use when designing or reviewing physical-keyboard navigation, Full Keyboard Access, standard or custom shortcuts, modifier behavior, and shortcut discoverability.
---

# Make commands discoverable and preserve familiar keys

Read [Keyboards](../../references/keyboards.md). Inspect task commands, text-entry contexts, current bindings, supported platforms/locales, and requested design/review/adaptation. Physical keyboards are covered on every listed platform except watchOS. Preserve the existing stack and identify actual keyboard evidence before claiming complete navigation.

Build a command inventory from frequent actions. Reuse familiar standard shortcuts for their expected meanings; consult the guide's mapping in context rather than treating legacy/system entries as universally available app APIs. A standard combination may serve another meaning only when its normal action has no place in this app. Avoid deriving an unrelated command by adding modifiers to a familiar one.

For app-specific commands, prefer a learnable Command-based combination, Shift for related variants, and sparing Option; avoid Control conflicts. Check international keyboards where Option makes characters. Preserve expected modifier-drag/resize behavior and clear smallest-increment arrow adjustment. Games may use single keys and customization while retaining system actions.

Trace ordinary content focus and Full Keyboard Access separately. On iPad, content/text/sidebar/collection focus is not proof that every button/switch is reachable; Full Keyboard Access supplies the broader route. Preserve accessibility shortcuts. On visionOS, make each Command-discoverability title meaningful without submenu context because the displayed list is flattened.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a diagram app uses Command-C to create a shape, binds Control-based shortcuts for everything, and has an unreachable Done button. Decision: copy semantics and a complete keyboard task outweigh shortcut novelty. After, Command-C copies selection, shape creation gets a suitable distinct command, and focus/activation can reach Done; the command title explains itself in discoverability UI.

Deliver a corrected command/binding inventory and keyboard task path or implementation. Fail if text editing invokes an unrelated command, shortcuts collide with system access, or the task cannot finish without a pointer. Actual OS shortcuts, international layouts, and Full Keyboard Access need supported-device execution; static binding inspection is narrower evidence.

Use [Focus and selection](../apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) for grouping/order or [Game controls](../apple-hig-game-controls/SKILL.md) for gameplay-specific bindings.

name: apple-hig-gestures
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting touch, indirect hand, direct spatial, trackpad, or Watch gestures and their discoverable alternatives.
---

# Make gestures predictable shortcuts to visible work

Read [Gestures](../../references/gestures.md). Inspect the task, target platforms, existing system/custom gestures, physical demands, and visible alternatives. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Preserve the stack; use actual interaction evidence to distinguish a gesture conflict from an untested possibility.

Start with standard meanings for tap, swipe, drag, hold, zoom, and rotation. Give immediate predictive feedback showing what moves, how far, and whether movement is locked/unavailable. Keep an explicit route for essential work through controls or supported alternative input. A custom gesture needs a frequent specialized task, simple explanation, discoverability, and another way to perform the action; if teaching it is harder than the task, redesign.

Check conflicts against the platform's reserved navigation, edges, undo/redo, multitasking, and overlay gestures. Do not repurpose a familiar system action to save one button. On visionOS, prioritize indirect interaction from rest and avoid sustained raised arms, complex two-hand/finger patterns, prescribed handedness, or required body movement. Custom hand gestures need Full Space/hand-data permission and must coexist with palm/wrist system overlays. On Watch, double tap already scrolls or advances vertical containers; only assign a primary button action where the container context permits it.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a spatial editor requires a two-hand twist above shoulder height to close a panel and places tool UI directly on the wrist. Decision: dismissal must be simple and compatible with system overlays. After, a labeled Close action and familiar indirect activation cover dismissal; optional manipulation gestures supplement visible controls, and task tools move away from reserved wrist space.

Deliver a gesture-to-action/conflict map and revised interaction artifact. Fail if an essential task has only a complex gesture, standard navigation changes meaning, feedback lags behind the manipulated content, or a system overlay competes for the same movement. Ergonomics and gesture recognition require real-use/device testing; static review cannot verify reliability.

Use [Accessibility](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for alternatives, [Apple Pencil and Scribble](../apple-hig-apple-pencil-and-scribble/SKILL.md) for stylus gestures, or [Eyes](../apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md) for indirect target feedback.

name: apple-hig-text-fields
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting short input fields, labels, validation, secure entry, formatting, and focus order.
---

# Preserve meaning while people enter a value

Read [the text-field guide](../../references/text-fields.md). This workflow is application advice; keep platform input capabilities and validation timing qualified.

Inspect value type, required format, sensitivity, labels, validation, target platform/input, and create/review/adapt request. Determine whether short entry is appropriate or a text view/choice control would reduce effort. Record actual format and commit rules rather than guessing from placeholder examples.

Keep purpose understandable after the placeholder disappears by adding persistent labels when necessary. Use secure entry for sensitive content and size/align fields to explain expected values and associations. Preserve logical Tab order. Validate at a useful moment: email often on leaving, creation feedback for username/password before leaving. Use understandable corrective feedback and locale-aware numeric formatters rather than punctuation-stripping shortcuts. Choose deliberate clipping/wrapping and an appropriate keyboard/content type. Offer trailing Clear on iOS/iPadOS; evaluate Mac combo boxes for suggestions plus custom values. Minimize typing on TV/watch and prefer existing choices where useful.

Implement fields/format/validation/focus or supply an input contract; reviews must identify the exact entered value and resulting failure. Do not broaden into account-security changes merely because a password field is present.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a price field labelled only by `$0.00` rejects a comma decimal after every keystroke and loses its label once entered. Decision: purpose and locale semantics must persist while partial input is allowed. After: use a persistent Price label, locale-aware currency representation, and validation that distinguishes intermediate entry from an invalid committed value.

Deliver the artifact and label, type, validation moment, feedback, formatting, and focus contract. Verify empty/partial/invalid/valid input, locale changes, secure content, Tab traversal, and long values. Fail for hidden purpose, exposed secrets, lost valid input, or format coercion changing meaning. Separate inspected logic from native keyboard/assistive execution.

Use [entering-data](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-entering-data/SKILL.md) for form strategy, [virtual-keyboards](../apple-hig-virtual-keyboards/SKILL.md) for entry layout, or [text-views](../../../apple-hig-content/.topics/apple-hig-text-views/SKILL.md) for extended content.

name: apple-hig-accessibility
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting Apple-platform interfaces for text enlargement, sensory access, assistive input, motor access, cognitive needs, or accessibility preferences.
---

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Preserve readable hierarchy as text grows

Read [Typography](../../references/typography.md). Inspect the actual text roles, font files/styles, platform, viewing context, and resizing behavior. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Use the guide's platform style/size tables when exact values matter; do not reproduce the entire specification or confuse its minimum with a comfortable default.

# Text fields Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-fields) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. Use a text field for a short, specific value such as a name or email address. A text view is the better primitive for extended text. ## Best practices - Explain purpose with a placeholder, and add a persistent external label where losing the placeholder during entry would make the field ambiguous. - Use secure entry for sensitive content. Size fields to suggest expected input length; stack groups with even spacing and consistent widths where possible so labels remain clearly associated. - Keep Tab traversal in the expected logical order, using system behavior unless a correction is needed. - Validate at a useful moment. Email validation often belongs when leaving the field; username/password creation feedback should occur before leaving it. Reject values incompatible with the required format with understandable feedback. - Use number formatters for numeric constraints and representations such as decimal precision, percentages, and currency, retaining locale-sensitive formatting. - Choose overflow behavior intentionally: system defaults clip, but character/word wrapping or beginning/middle/end ellipses may better fit the task. An expansion tooltip can reveal full clipped content to a pointer user. - Select the appropriate virtual keyboard for iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, and visionOS. Minimize both field count and lengthy entry on tvOS and watchOS; choices or buttons can gather information more efficiently. ## Platform considerations No additional tvOS or visionOS rules are specified. ### iOS, iPadOS Offer a trailing Clear control to erase the current value in one action. Leading imagery can explain purpose; trailing buttons can offer extra functionality, such as bookmarking. ### macOS A combo box is useful when free typing should coexist with a predefined set of likely choices. ### watchOS Request typed text only when necessary; prefer selecting an existing option. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Text views](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-views) [Combo boxes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/combo-boxes) [Entering data](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/entering-data) #### Developer documentation — SwiftUI — SwiftUI — UIKit — AppKit ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 5, 2023.

# Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Typography Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Ensuring legibility](#Ensuring-legibility) - [Conveying hierarchy](#Conveying-hierarchy) - [Using system fonts](#Using-system-fonts) - [Using custom fonts](#Using-custom-fonts) - [Supporting Dynamic Type](#Supporting-Dynamic-Type) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) ## Ensuring legibility Test type at real viewing distances, lighting conditions, and supported devices. Enlarge hard-to-read text, improve foreground/background contrast, or choose a more legible face. Prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold over Ultralight/Thin/Light, especially at small sizes. Thin custom faces often need sizes above the recommendations. |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| ## Conveying hierarchy Combine size, weight, and color to distinguish levels, and preserve those relationships as text grows. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Runtime tracking adapts by size automatically; mockups may need the tracking values below. ## Using custom fonts Check custom faces against platform size recommendations and actual conditions. Implement Dynamic Type and Bold Text behavior equivalent to the system faces. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can support Dynamic Type in games; if unsuitable, offer a separate text-size adjustment. ## Supporting Dynamic Type Dynamic Type is available in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Test every supported size, including Larger Accessibility Text on iPhone/iPad. Scale meaningful glyphs as well as text; SF Symbols integrate automatically. Preserve useful information at the largest accessibility size rather than aggressively truncating. Give labels enough lines and avoid truncation in scrolling regions unless a detail view exposes the full text. Stack inline timestamps/glyphs beneath or above primary text, grow containers, and reduce columns when width becomes cramped. Keep important content toward the top and the overall hierarchy stable. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS SF Pro is standard; New York is also available. ### macOS SF Pro is standard and New York is available to Mac Catalyst apps. macOS has no Dynamic Type. Match standard-control typography with the relevant NSFont methods: `controlContentFont`, `labelFont`, `menuFont`, `menuBarFont`, `messageFont`, `paletteFont`, `titleBarFont`, `toolTipsFont`, `userFont`, `userFixedPitchFont`, `boldSystemFont`, and `systemFont`, each with its `ofSize:` parameter. ### tvOS SF Pro is standard, with New York also available. ### visionOS SF Pro is standard; specify text styles explicitly when using New York. Body/title Dynamic Type styles are bolder, and Extra Large Title 1/2 support wide editorial compositions. Prefer readable 2D text with little or no extrusion. Test full-scale designs through different viewing scales. Default white text contrasts with glass; test custom colors against diverse surroundings. Without a container background, bold can improve visibility; do not rely on unpredictable cast shadows. Billboard labels associated with 3D objects toward the viewer, normally rotating around the y-axis so the baseline stays perpendicular to the line of sight. ### watchOS SF Compact is standard, New York is available, and complications use SF Compact Rounded. ## Specifications Values below preserve the source’s factual measurements. Sizes, leading, and line heights are in points; tracking is given in thousandths of an em and points. Emphasis can be applied through SwiftUI `bold()` or UIKit `UIFontDescriptor` `traitBold`; the resulting emphasized weight varies by style. Use semantic APIs in production instead of freezing all layout to these reference values.

item.text: The brief identifies three problems to resolve: Pencil proximity blocks typing, specimen IDs require handwriting, and one gesture can erase ink or delete a page. The revised specification will keep input methods available together, separate text from ink, and give page deletion an explicit, reversible action.

# Revised iPad laboratory notebook interaction specification

## Scope and decisions

This is a framework-agnostic design contract for the iPadOS notebook described in "'`interface.md`. Apple Pencil is optional. The supplied artifact is a behavior description, not an implementation. Requirements below are proposed product decisions; HIG support is cited separately. No Apple SDK is assumed.

| Supplied behavior | Revised decision | Reason and source |
|---|---|---|
| Typing is disabled when Pencil is nearby | Proximity changes neither text availability nor focus, selection, keyboard visibility, or document content. Typing, paste, touch, and Pencil can alternate within the same task. | Pencil should support ordinary control activation and mixed writing tasks; hover must never activate content. [Pencil: Best practices, Hover](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pencil-and-scribble) |
| Specimen IDs require handwriting | Store IDs as editable text. Offer onscreen keyboard, hardware keyboard, paste, and optional handwriting-to-text. Never require recognition to complete entry. | Text fields suit short specific values; preserve keyboard entry and familiar editing. [Text fields](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-fields), [Keyboards](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards) |
| One gesture erases ink and deletes pages | Erasing affects ink only. Remove the page-deletion interpretation entirely. Provide a separate labeled “Delete page” action with cancellation and recovery. | Keep gestures predictable and provide visible alternatives; Pencil hardware gestures should be nondestructive and reversible. [Gestures](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gestures), [Pencil: Double tap, Squeeze](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pencil-and-scribble) |
| Text boxes are custom canvases | Retain a drawing surface for ink; replace short-value text canvases with semantic editable text controls, or an adapter satisfying the text contract below. Rendering text on a canvas alone is insufficient. | Standard editable text supports Scribble automatically in supported environments; custom fields need explicit handwriting behavior. This does not establish support in the eventual framework. [Pencil: Scribble](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pencil-and-scribble), [Accessibility: Mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) |

## Surface and data contract

A page contains a persistently labeled “Specimen ID” text field and a separate labeled “Ink notes” drawing region including useful margins. Keep their hit regions distinct: writing in the ID region edits text; writing in the drawing region creates ink. No stroke may fall through from a field into the drawing region. A stroke retains its original target until it ends. Other existing text content must retain its values when migrated out of canvas rendering.

Use visible Pen, Eraser, Undo, Redo, and Delete page actions. Show the active drawing tool with both a name and selected state. Pencil can activate these controls. Finger dragging in the drawing region scrolls by default; an explicit “Draw with finger” option enables finger marking for people without Pencil. While that option is active, provide a visible Scroll action to restore navigation. Essential text and page operations never depend on drawing ability.

For controls, start with iPadOS activation areas of 44 × 44 pt, with separation preventing overlap; this is a product target based on the guide’s default, not a claim about measured geometry. Keep tools clear of either writing hand and allow repositioning. Use body text at the iPadOS 17 pt default with semantic sizing or equivalent. At 200% text scale and supported larger accessibility sizes, grow and stack controls and labels; preserve full ID access through editing/scrolling rather than ellipsis alone. [Accessibility: Vision, Mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility), [Typography: Supporting Dynamic Type](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography)

### Specimen ID field

- Representation: an exact text string, not a number; preserve leading zeros, case, punctuation, and entered Unicode. Disable automatic capitalization, spelling correction, and smart punctuation for this identifier. Offer an alphanumeric entry layout where available, never a digits-only restriction.
- Purpose: persistent “Specimen ID” label; placeholder is optional and hides as writing begins. A trailing “Clear specimen ID” control clears only the draft and is undoable.
- Editing: caret, range selection, copy, cut, paste, deletion, and undo work across input methods. Changing inputs preserves the draft, caret, selection, and committed value. Handwriting recognition updates the same draft; it does not silently commit an ID.
- Commit: explicit “Apply specimen ID” or Return validates and commits. Leaving the field retains the draft without silently applying it. “Cancel ID edit” restores the last committed value and ends editing. Page navigation retains drafts so a failed or interrupted edit is recoverable.
- Validation: require a nonempty, non-whitespace-only value on Apply. Keep the draft and show “Enter a specimen ID” next to the field if invalid; do not clear it or trap focus. Apply stays available so its failure can be explained. No laboratory format, length limit, uniqueness rule, or registry is supplied; impose none in this specification. A whitespace-containing nonblank ID is preserved, not trimmed. Any later laboratory rule must have explicit corrective feedback before commit.
- Long values remain editable end to end without clipping data. Locale/input-source changes never parse the ID as a localized number or transform its characters. These are ordinary identifiers; no supplied evidence establishes a need for password-style masking.

These validation and commit rules are product decisions, informed by [Text fields: Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/text-fields).

## Interaction and state model

Track independently: `textDraft`, `committedID`, `textSelection`, `focusedTarget`, `drawingTool`, `activeStrokeTarget`, `pendingTranscription`, `pageDeletionState`, and reversible document edits. Pencil availability is capability metadata, never an edit lock.

| Event/context | Required transition and feedback |
|---|---|
| Pencil approaches, leaves, disconnects, or hovers | Preserve all editing state. Supported hover may preview the likely ink mark inside the ink region only; never write, commit, focus, erase, or delete. |
| Tap ID with finger/Pencil; keyboard navigation enters ID | Enter text editing. A finger tap offers the onscreen keyboard when appropriate; hardware typing remains available. Pencil activation must not disable the explicit keyboard route. |
| Pencil writes in ID target, handwriting supported | Begin without a preliminary focus tap. Hide placeholder. Freeze field position, transcription position, and writing-area geometry while writing/selection is active. Convert into editable draft text; defer reflow or scrolling until a writing pause and selection has ended. |
| Handwriting unavailable or recognition fails | Keep existing text intact. Offer “Use keyboard” and paste. Explain unavailable handwriting without presenting the field as unavailable. Do not create a fake transcription or silently save raw strokes as the ID. |
| Pencil contacts ink region with Pen | Begin drawing immediately without first selecting Pen for every stroke. Initial drawing tool is Pen; an explicitly chosen Eraser remains active until changed. Feedback follows contact; useful margins also accept marks. |
| Eraser stroke | Remove only intersecting ink strokes on the current page, grouped as one undoable edit per eraser stroke. Never remove text, page metadata, or the page, even when all ink is gone. |
| Pending handwriting plus another edit/Apply | Serialize edits to avoid late recognition overwriting newer typing. Apply waits for the active text composition to finish; show “Finishing handwriting…” while pending. Cancel invalidates its recognition token. Discard late results for canceled or superseded drafts. |
| Tool change during a stroke | Queue the change until stroke end; do not reinterpret an in-progress stroke. |
| Undo / Redo | Reverse/reapply the most recent edit in the active editing context; the action label identifies the operation, such as “Undo erase ink.” Field undo edits its draft. Outside field editing, document undo includes ink edits and page deletion. |

If supported by actual hardware, honor the person’s preferred Pencil double-tap tool mapping when applicable, including no action. Do not add a custom override by default. Squeeze may show quick tool choices near the tip as one discrete action; it never deletes or erases content directly. Barrel roll may affect a meaningful mark property, never navigation. Pressure and tilt may affect mark qualities, but neither is required for a legible mark or essential action. All hardware features require capability checks and have visible alternatives. [Pencil guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/apple-pencil-and-scribble)

### Separate page deletion

Activating “Delete page” identifies the current page and asks “Delete this page and its contents?” with Cancel and Delete page actions. Cancel is the initial safe action and preserves the page, draft, selection, and drawing tool. Confirmed deletion moves a complete page snapshot, including drafts and ink, into a recoverable deleted-pages store; it does not permanently purge it. Select the next page, otherwise the previous page, otherwise an empty-notebook view with Add page. Expose a persistent “Page deleted” status with Undo and a labeled “Deleted pages” recovery route. Recovery is not dependent on a timed toast. Undo restores the page at its prior position with its content; Redo repeats the recoverable deletion. Permanent purge is outside this specification.

This confirmation and recovery policy is a product choice to protect notebook content, not a universal HIG requirement. In an eventual Assistive Access adaptation, any difficult-to-reverse deletion must follow the local guide’s two-confirmation condition. [Accessibility: Cognitive](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility)

## Keyboard, gesture, and alternative access contract

Preserve ordinary text gestures and system undo/redo, copy/paste, app switching, edge navigation, and multitasking gestures. Do not reuse the former ambiguous erasing gesture for a second operation. Eraser is an explicit tool; no hidden page-deletion gesture remains. Offer visible Undo and Redo even when a compact drawing palette omits them. [Gestures: iOS, iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gestures)

Use Command-C/X/V/A for normal text selection editing and Command-Z / Shift-Command-Z for Undo/Redo in context. Delete/Backspace in text edits text only; outside text it never deletes a page. Escape cancels a pending deletion or ID edit. Do not introduce a page-deletion shortcut. Keep the standard editing commands discoverable without overriding system accessibility shortcuts. [Keyboards](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards)

Ordinary iPad keyboard content navigation enters the page content group with Specimen ID as its primary item. Tab/Shift-Tab traverse logical content groups; arrows navigate within appropriate custom groups and retain text-caret semantics inside the field. Full Keyboard Access must separately reach and activate every tool, Apply, Cancel, Clear, Delete, confirmation, and recovery control. Ordinary content focus alone is insufficient evidence of that access. Focus must remain distinct from selected drawing tool and selected page. Return from canceled deletion restores its invoker. [Focus and selection: iPadOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection)

Expose the ID as an editable-text role with label, exact value, required state, and associated validation feedback. Expose actions with names, button roles, availability, and selected tool state where applicable. Ink notes has a named drawing region; tool and recovery actions remain reachable without drawing gestures. Error and deletion statuses use text, not color or sound alone. Complete the ID-entry and page-recovery task with keyboard and supported assistive input; handwriting is optional. Detailed spoken order and actual assistive behavior remain implementation verification work. [Accessibility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility)

## Worked before/after

Example data `AB-0017` is illustrative, not an inferred laboratory format.
